description: Pin capability tables for schematic pin-swap feedback (pcbpilot pcb auto run → feedback.json → sch pin-swap). A pin is a swap slot only when it carries the 'gpio' capability and no 'fixed' reason. Canonical copy: .agents/skills/pcbpilot/references/pin-capabilities.json; pkg/pcbauto/data/pin-capabilities.json is the embedded mirror (a test keeps them identical).

schema.parts[].match: case-insensitive substrings of the PCB device / part name
schema.parts[].remap: gpio-matrix = any digital function (GPIO, UART, I2C, SPI ≤ 40 MHz, LEDC/PWM, RMT) can be routed to any gpio pin; af-table = only plain GPIO nets move freely, a peripheral net needs every non-gpio capability of its current pin on the target pin (STM32/AT32 alternate-function tables)
schema.parts[].pins[]: {pin: footprint pad number, name, gpio?: number, caps: [gpio, adc1, adc2, touch, dac, usart1_tx, …], fixed?: why the pin must not move, caution?: why a swap onto it needs a human check}
schema.netNeeds[]: {pattern: Go regexp on the net name, needs: capability every candidate pin must carry} — first match wins; no match = plain digital
schema.genericConnectors: headers whose signal pins are interchangeable (power/ground pins stay): match on device/name, exclude protocol connectors

parts.source: Espressif ESP32-S3-WROOM-1/1U datasheet (pin definitions, strapping pins) + ESP32-S3 TRM ch. IO MUX and GPIO matrix
notes: ADC2 is unusable while Wi-Fi is active: an analog net that must work with Wi-Fi needs adc1 (declare the net name with ADC1 or keep it off ADC2 pins)
Pins 28–30 (IO35–37) are reserved for octal PSRAM on R8 variants and treated as fixed for every variant
